t: 3211. Generate Binary Strings Without Adjacent Zeros
o: Generate all length-n binary strings containing no "00" substring. For n=3 there are five such strings; for n=1 both "0" and "1" qualify. With n <= 18 there are at most 2^18 = 262144 strings, so even full enumeration is fine.
k: Validity is local: a '0' may only be followed by '1'.
Backtracking grows strings character by character, pruning invalid branches early; bitmask enumeration is a simpler brute-force alternative.

a.i: Build strings left to right. Always append '1'; append '0' only if the previous character is not '0'. This prunes the invalid "00" branches immediately and generates exactly the valid strings.
s: Recurse with the current string and the last appended character.
Always branch on appending '1'; branch on '0' only if last != '0'.
When the length reaches n, record the string.
a.t: O(2^n) worst case — the number of valid strings is Fibonacci-like, so actual output size is smaller

a.i: Every candidate string corresponds to an integer mask below 2^n. Format each mask as a binary string of length n and reject it if it contains "00". Simple and hard to get wrong, at the cost of examining all 2^n masks.
s: Convert to an n-bit binary string; keep it iff it does not contain "00".
a.t: O(2^n · n) — each of 2^n masks is formatted and scanned
a.sp: O(n) auxiliary per string, plus output

w: Backtracking is preferable for larger n since it only visits valid prefixes; enumeration wins on simplicity. Edge cases: n=1 returns both strings. A follow-up: count valid strings without generating them — that is a linear DP with states ending in '0'/'1' (Fibonacci numbers).
